content.text: Section 20 fully covers the preferred position. Submitting a compliant finding.

input.quote: 20.2 Vendor shall also defend, indemnify, and hold harmless the Customer indemnified parties from third-party claims to the extent arising from Vendor's breach of Applicable Law; bodily injury, death, or tangible property damage caused by Vendor; unauthorized access to or disclosure of Customer Data caused by Vendor; or Vendor's gross negligence, wilful misconduct, or fraud.
input.rationale: Section 20 meets the preferred position in full. Clause 20.1 gives an unqualified Vendor defence and indemnity for third-party IP infringement/misappropriation claims covering Customer, its Affiliates and their personnel; 20.2 adds Vendor's breach of Applicable Law, bodily injury/property damage, unauthorised access to or disclosure of Customer Data caused by Vendor, and Vendor's gross negligence, wilful misconduct and fraud. Clause 20.4 sets out standard procedure (prompt notice with material-prejudice qualifier, cooperation at the indemnifying Party's expense, control of defence, and settlement consent protections). Clause 20.5 provides the infringement remedies (procure, modify/replace, or terminate with refund) as an addition to, not a substitute for, the defence obligation. The Customer indemnity in 20.3 is appropriately narrow — limited to unmodified Customer-supplied material used strictly as authorised and Customer's violation of Applicable Law, with carve-outs for Vendor Technology, modifications, combinations and Vendor instructions. Indemnification obligations are also "Excluded Claims" under 21.3, so the Vendor indemnity is not swallowed by the general liability cap (better than the fallback 3× super-cap). No redline required.
